program.title: Volleyball Outside Hitter: Jump & Landing Power Week 1

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Intermediate volleyball outside hitter (left side) with mild occasional landing discomfort in knee. Single gym session per week (60 min), moderate stress, good sleep. Primary goal: sport performance and jump height.
primary_constraints: Mild knee landing discomfort—prioritize low-impact loading, hip/trunk control, landing mechanics only if pain-free
1 session/week requires high density and sport specificity to drive volleyball performance
60-minute session limits main work to 4 exercises max
sport_demands: Outside hitter needs explosive vertical jump, deceleration control, and repeated jumping capacity
Transition attacks require hip extension power, trunk rotation, and landing stability
Passing and serve-receive require hip mobility, low posture endurance, and lateral movement
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Build foundational jump-power strength and landing safety through posterior-chain loading (squat pattern, hinge pattern, calf capacity) combined with core anti-rotation control. Avoid high-impact plyometrics until landing mechanics prove stable and pain-free.

weeks.theme: Squat pattern strength + hinge + core stiffness for jump foundation

workouts.title: Jump Power Foundation: Squat + Hinge + Core
adaptation_targets: Hip extension power for vertical jump
sport_transfer: Squat strength drives approach and jump power in attacks and blocks
Hip extension and calf strength support vertical jump height and landing control
Core bracing stabilizes trunk rotation during serving and hitting transitions
workouts.why_this_session: Build bilateral squat and posterior-chain strength while protecting the knee through controlled loading, low-impact movement, and adductor/calf capacity work.

warmup.name: Bird Dog
warmup.purpose: Activate core stability and spinal control before loading.

warmup.name: Lateral Band Walk
warmup.purpose: Activate hip abductors and prepare knees for squat control.

warmup.name: Deep Squat Pry
warmup.purpose: Open hips and ankles; establish squat depth cues.

main_work.name: Box Squat
main_work.purpose: Controlled bilateral squat with standardized depth; knee-friendly mechanics for jump power.
main_work.load_guidance: RPE 6–7 (medium-heavy); prioritize controlled descent and pause. Avoid pain.
main_work.tempo: 3 sec descent, 1 sec pause, 1 sec ascent

main_work.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
main_work.purpose: Centered-load hinge to build posterior-chain power while reducing knee stress.
main_work.load_guidance: RPE 6–7; maintain balanced foot pressure and neutral spine throughout.

main_work.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
main_work.purpose: Unilateral calf and ankle capacity for landing stability and jump power.
main_work.load_guidance: Hold dumbbell in one hand if balance allows; light load OK.
main_work.tempo: 2 sec rise, 1 sec hold, 2 sec lower

main_work.name: RKC Plank
main_work.purpose: Maximal-tension core bracing for trunk stiffness and anti-extension control.
main_work.load_guidance: Full-body tension; pull elbows toward toes without arm movement.

cooldown.name: Dead Bug
cooldown.purpose: Supine core control and low-back recovery.

cooldown.name: Cable Hip Adduction
cooldown.purpose: Adductor tissue capacity for landing stability and injury prevention.
cooldown.load_guidance: Light load; focus on control and inner-thigh activation.

injury_modifications: If knee pain during box squat: reduce depth by 2–3 cm or sit on higher box; monitor hip and ankle mobility
If calf raise pain: reduce range of motion or use support; prioritize single-leg control over height
If plank causes discomfort: reduce duration to 20–25 sec or elevate hands on bench to lower spine load

weeks.progression_rule: Establish baseline loads (moderate weight, RPE 6–7) for 5–6 reps per set. Monitor knee comfort during landing prep drills. Progress next week if no pain escalation.

program.nutrition_focus: Post-session protein intake (20–30 g) and carbohydrates (30–40 g) within 1–2 hours to support muscle recovery and jump adaptation. Maintain consistent hydration during week.
recovery_focus: Sleep target: maintain 7+ hours nightly to support strength and power adaptation
Stress management: use low-intensity movement (walking, easy mobility) on non-training days to reduce moderate stress level
Avoid high-intensity conditioning outside session; focus recovery on sleep and nutrition this week
safety_notes: Do not perform depth jumps, box jumps, or plyometrics until landing mechanics are pain-free and have been cleared in follow-up sessions
Knee pain during any exercise signals immediate exercise modification or cessation; report changes to coach or healthcare provider
Do not max-load or test 1RM with existing knee discomfort
assumptions: Athlete has access to trap bar or can substitute with safety bar squat if trap bar unavailable
Athlete can perform all exercises without acute pain; soreness is normal
One session per week is the total dedicated strength block; sport-specific drills and match play are separate
Athlete has moderate recovery capacity and will focus on sleep and stress management outside this session
